column1: ## One more reading for E6: x sd against the uniform disc

column2: detail

a crowd spread evenly over a disc of radius R has a standard deviation of R/2 along any diameter. R is 26.46 m here, so the uniform value is 13.23 m, and the seeds read 12.83 to 14.30 m at the three times. Round 38's disc was 11.28 m, uniform 5.64 m, and it read 5.43 to 5.77 m. Both worlds fill their disc; round 39's tank is not more concentrated than round 38's, it is simply five and a half times wider.

the footer prints -69.16 to -70.32 m while the map over the disc bottoms out at -59.9 to -60.7 m. The difference is SeaFloor.SeamMarginMetres, 5 m of skirt on every side of the bounding square, on which the unclamped map keeps falling down the ramp. The rebuilt map reproduces every bed field run.json records exactly, so this is the mesh's extent and not a disagreement about the floor.

column1: ## The seeds split in two on the growth dials, and the split predates the eaters

column2: detail

seeds 1 and 2 carry adult scale 0.61 to 0.77, investment 0.27, brood 2.6 to 3.4 and body frac 0.91 to 0.95; seeds 3, 4 and 5 carry adult scale 0.29 to 0.32, investment 0.44 to 0.73, brood 1.0 to 2.2 and body frac 0.98 to 1.00. The split is already there at 5,000 s, before any seed has eaters, so the body plan came first. Seeds 1 and 2 are the two that still hold an absorptive clade at 30,000 s and the two that pass the goal rule. n is five, and this is a correlation and not a mechanism. Round 38's five all read adult scale 0.24 to 0.27 at the end, so round 39's seeds 1 and 2 evolved larger adults than any round 38 seed did.
